Title: DAP leaders considered resigning before settling on Loke's exit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The decision for DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke to resign as Transport Minister was not easily reached, with several party leaders prepared to step down, said DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) member Syahredzan Johan.
He said the CEC had thoroughly considered the implications before deciding that Loke's resignation was the best course of action.
"The committee agreed that while DAP respects the discretion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong in the Pardons Board, Loke would resign as minister to uphold the party's commitment to fighting corruption and abuse of power," he said in a statement.
Earlier, Loke announced that he
would resign from the cabinet
following the Pardons Board's decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest.
Loke said the party's other ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the government.
"After discussions and taking into account the reactions from the CEC, I will resign as transport minister, while the rest will remain in the government," he told reporters at DAP headquarters in Jalan Pudu today.
Syahredzan said Loke would step down after settling several pending matters at the ministry.
"At the same time, all other DAP ministers and deputy ministers will remain in their positions to ensure political stability and prevent political opponents from gaining an advantage," he said.
He said the decision followed a three-hour CEC meeting held in response to the Pardons Board's decision yesterday.
Wanita DAP chief Teo Nie Ching said the decision was not made lightly after three hours of "intense deliberation".
"Loke's courage and wisdom in making a bold decision at this critical moment speak volumes about his leadership and also reflect DAP's long-standing principle," she said.
She also urged the government to disclose the official minutes of the Pardons Board meeting in the interest of transparency and public accountability.
"The public deserves complete clarity on the considerations and processes that led to this decision," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar joins 20,000 at Sarong Music Run
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined about 20,000 participants at the Malaysia Sarong Music Run 2026 here today.
Anwar, who opened the event at Kuala Lumpur City Centre, later walked with participants from the Petronas Twin Towers to Pavilion Kuala Lumpur.
He was accompanied by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing.
Before flagging off the run, Anwar urged participants to remain active and take care of their health.
"Thank you everyone, young and old, women and men. Keep up the spirit of looking after your health, stay healthy and take care of the country," he said.
The event featured 3km and 5km runs, drawing about 20,000 participants from Malaysia and abroad.
This year's programme also featured a 2km Jalur Gemilang procession, while singer Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza made a special appearance to lead the Rukun Negara recitation.
Hisam Hasim, 49, a Singaporean civil servant, said he travelled to Kuala Lumpur specifically to take part in the event after learning about it through social media.
An avid runner, Hisam took part in the 5km category and said the event allowed him to experience the strong sense of patriotism among Malaysians.
"I could really feel the Malaysian spirit and patriotism throughout the event. It was a great atmosphere and something special to experience," he said.
He said another highlight was seeing Siti Nurhaliza and Anwar in person.
"I was excited to see Siti Nurhaliza and the prime minister in the flesh. It made the experience even more memorable," he said.
Meanwhile, Muhammad Syarifuddin Qadar, 18, said the event marked his first participation in an organised run.
Syarifuddin, who is awaiting his next college intake, said he initially took up running to improve his cardiovascular fitness for combat sports but gradually developed a passion for it.
"At first, I ran to improve my cardio because combat sports require good endurance. But the more I ran, the more I started enjoying it. There is a sense of freedom when I run," he said.
Syarifuddin, who participated in the 3km category, said the experience had encouraged him to take part in more running events in future.
"This is my first run, and I will definitely join more running events after this," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Croatian climber fined RM25,000 for illegal Mount Kinabalu entry
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Croatian mountain climber Mauro Persic has been issued the maximum RM25,000 compound for illegally entering Mount Kinabalu.
The 46-year-old paid the compound after Sabah Parks enforcement personnel briefed him on the offence and provisions and penalties under the Parks Enactment 1984 (Amendment 2024).
The proceedings were conducted at the Operations Control Centre of the Operations and Enforcement Office at Sabah Parks headquarters here.
He was released after paying the compound in full, with all matters related to the case completed.
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin was quoted in a news report as saying that Sabah Parks had also informed the Ranau police of the development for record-keeping and any further action.
Earlier this month, Persic entered Mount Kinabalu through the Mesilou River via an unauthorised route without a permit before falling and suffering leg and rib injuries.
More than 40 personnel
from multiple agencies were involved in a five-day search and rescue operation after he alerted the authorities.
Persic has since apologised to the local community, acknowledging that he had failed to give sufficient thought and consideration before embarking on the climb.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rompin cops urge other victims of alleged school assault to come forward
Article:
ROMPIN: Police have urged parents of students at a religious school here to lodge reports if their children have been bullied, following an allegation made by a mother today.
Rompin deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohamad Zamri Mohamad Zaber said police had so far received only two reports regarding the incident, which occurred at the school hostel on Sept 12.
"If there are any other incidents or students who have been victimised, come and lodge a report. We will investigate," he said when contacted today.
He was commenting on claims by Siti Rohani Yusof, 40, whose
son was among two students
allegedly assaulted by five senior students at the school hostel on Sept 12.
She claimed that more than 10 other students had previously been assaulted by the same seniors, but the incidents were never reported.
Meanwhile, Zamri said the Sept 12 incident involving the
two Form Two students
was the first bullying case reported at the religious school.
He said police had also recorded statements from the school management, including the warden, as well as the five suspects accused of injuring the two victims, both aged 14.
Zamri said the five suspects, aged between 16 and 17, had been released on police bail.
The case is being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting, which carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Earlier, Siti Rohani told a press conference that the incident had left her family traumatised after the suspects allegedly hit her son with a broomstick and threatened him with a penknife.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Igal-Igal festival proposed as annual event across Tun Sakaran Marine Park
Article:
SEMPORNA: The inaugural Igal-Igal Festival at Mantabuan Island here has been proposed as an annual community-based event that could be expanded to other islands within Tun Sakaran Marine Park (TSMP).
State Tourism, Culture and Environment Ministry deputy permanent secretary Rimi Repin said the initiative could provide island communities with a platform to showcase their cultural heritage, traditions and tourism products.
She said Igal-Igal represented more than a traditional dance, describing it as
part of the Bajau community's heritage
, identity and pride.
"Igal-Igal is among the cultural treasures that hold their own unique value and have been passed down from generation to generation.
"The beauty of its dance movements, accompanied by traditional music and its distinctive performances, reflects the richness of the culture and creativity of the local community.
"We want Igal-Igal to be recognised not only among the local community, but also introduced to visitors from Malaysia and abroad as part of Semporna's cultural identity.
"I welcome this aspiration because community-based programmes have the potential to become an ongoing platform for promoting cultural heritage and the unique tourism attractions of the marine park areas," she said when officiating the two-day 2026 Igal-Igal Festival at Mantabuan Island here today.
The inaugural festival was organised by the Mantabuan Island community and Koperasi Alam Laut Silangau Semporna Berhad (KOPSI), with Brand Borneo Tours, Travel and Experiences Sdn Bhd as co-organiser, in collaboration with the Tun Sakaran Marine Park management and relevant agencies.
Mantabuan is one of eight islands under Tun Sakaran Marine Park. The others are Bohey Dulang, Bodgaya, Tetagan, Selakan, Sebangkat, Maiga and Sibuan.
Rimi said activities featured in the festival, including environmental awareness programmes, arts and cultural exhibitions, traditional music, traditional food and community activities, could help raise awareness about protecting the islands and marine ecosystems.
She said expanding the festival to other islands, with the cooperation of all stakeholders, could create opportunities for more island communities to participate in tourism-related economic activities.
These could include handicraft production, traditional food preparation, tourism services and other supporting activities.
However, Rimi said the success of an annual festival should not be measured solely by visitor numbers or the vibrancy of the event.
"It should also be measured by the benefits returned to the community and its impact on the preservation of cultural heritage and the environment," she said.
Rimi also stressed the importance of ensuring that tourism development in Tun Sakaran Marine Park was carried out responsibly and sustainably.
"We cannot separate tourism development from our responsibility to protect the environment," she said.
Also present were marine park manager Ghazali Pe Hindi and co-organisers Jasni Kanti and Anton Ngui.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Loke will resign as minister [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Transport Minister Anthony Loke will resign from the cabinet following the Pardons Board's decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, said the party's other ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the government.
"After discussions and taking into account the reactions from the CEC (Central Executive Committee), I will resign as transport minister, while the rest will remain in the government," he told reporters at DAP headquarters in Jalan Pudu today.
Loke announced his decision after a three-hour CEC meeting to discuss the party's stance on Najib's conditional house arrest.
He said he would formally tender his resignation letter to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in due course.
Loke said his decision to step down was a personal stance, while the other ministers would remain in their positions to maintain political stability.
"If all DAP ministers were to resign, the government could collapse, leading to political instability, which is precisely what our opponents are waiting for.
"DAP would not allow opposition forces to exploit the situation," he said.
Loke said DAP respected the royal prerogative exercised by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, but that the decision remained difficult for the party and the public to accept given the scale of the 1MDB scandal.
"The 1MDB scandal is a major corruption crisis that has plagued the nation for a decade.
"DAP has always fought for truth and justice, and those responsible must face the full weight of the law," he said.
He also assured the public that operations at the Transport Ministry and ongoing national infrastructure projects would continue without disruption during the transition.
Yesterday, the
Federal Territories Pardons Board
announced that Najib, 73, had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
The decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya at Istana Negara.
​The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.
Najib, the former Pekan member of parliament, is currently serving a jail sentence over seven charges of criminal breach of trust, abuse of power and money laundering involving more than RM42 million belonging to SRC International.
He was convicted on all charges by the High Court in July 2020 following a lengthy trial and sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million.
Najib began serving his sentence on Aug 23, 2022, after the Court of Appeal and Federal Court dismissed his appeals and upheld his conviction.
On Jan 29, 2024, the Pardons Board halved his 12-year prison sentence to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
Yesterday's decision allows Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine.

Title: New e-commerce Bill expected to be finalised this year
Article:
BATU KAWAN: The government aims to finalise the drafting of a new e-commerce Bill this year, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the ministry had approved a policy decision to repeal the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 and replace it with a new, more comprehensive law.
However, he said the process would require coordination between ministries and extensive engagement with stakeholders, including e-commerce platforms, service providers and industry players.
"We know that e-commerce is a broad and comprehensive area, so it requires extensive engagement with stakeholders. We need to examine the matter thoroughly, and I hope it can be finalised," he told reporters after launching the 2026 Consumer Festival (CONFEST 2026) at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Armizan said two committees had also been established to expedite the drafting of the Bill, including to facilitate coordination between the ministry, the Communications Ministry and the Digital Ministry.
He said matters currently being fine-tuned included the division of responsibilities among the ministries and relevant agencies, as well as regulatory mechanisms for e-commerce platforms.
The next stage would require a regulatory impact assessment (RIA) in collaboration with the Malaysia Productivity Corporation (MPC) before the Bill is submitted for further consideration.
Among the proposals being studied is the introduction of a licensing regime for e-commerce platforms, particularly in view of the influx of goods from overseas, consumer safety and the sustainability of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
However, Armizan said regulation must be balanced to avoid hampering the growth of the e-commerce sector, which provides convenience to consumers and serves as a source of income for traders.
"We want more comprehensive and conducive regulation, but at the same time, we do not want to hamper the growth of e-commerce," he said.
The government had previously expressed its intention to expedite the drafting of the e-commerce Bill to strengthen the regulation and accountability of platforms, sellers and consumers, given that the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 does not provide a comprehensive legal framework to regulate various aspects of e-commerce.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Unity govt party ties still good, Zahid says after Najib granted house arrest
Article:
JAKARTA: Ties between parties in the unity government remain good following the Pardons Board's decision to grant
Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest,
says Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Zahid said the decision by the Pardons Board, chaired by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, was constitutional.
"Certainly, His Majesty has taken various aspects into consideration, and if any party wants to question the King's decision, then it would not be in line with the provisions of the Federal Constitution," he told a press conference.
He said Umno and Barisan Nasional maintained that the law must always be adhered to, adding that this was clear from his previous statements.
"Our relationship (with other parties in the unity government) is still good.
"We may be politicians, but when it comes to administrative matters, we are professional and there are no problems because decisions made by the Cabinet are a collective responsibility."
He said ties between Cabinet members were also good on a personal level.
His comments come amid mixed reactions to the conditional house arrest granted to former prime minister Najib.
Umno yesterday welcomed the Pardons Board's decision and began fundraising for the RM50 million fine Najib must pay to be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
Last night, the
Pakatan Harapan Presidential Council
said no one was above the law and that anyone convicted of an offence must serve their sentence in accordance with the Federal Constitution and the law.
The council said it stood firmly behind Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's position, as well as the advice given by the Attorney-General and Federal Territories Minister to the Pardons Board.
Earlier today, Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said it was inappropriate for anyone to portray the exercise of the constitutional power of pardon as an act of being "above the law".

Title: 14 banks begin offering reducing balance method for hire purchase
Article:
BATU KAWAN: Fourteen of the 20 banking institutions providing hire-purchase financing had begun offering customers the reducing balance method as of Sept 18, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the remaining six banking institutions were expected to complete the transition to the new method by Dec 31 at the latest, following engagement sessions with the banks.
"In total, there are 429 entities, comprising banking institutions and hire-purchase providers, registered with the Association of Hire Purchase Companies Malaysia," he told reporters at the closing ceremony of the Consumer Festival (CONFEST) 2026 at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Armizan added that the ministry had set a target for 80 per cent of hire-purchase providers to offer financing in compliance with the Hire-Purchase (Amendment) Act 2026 by the end of this year.
He said hire-purchase providers that were not yet fully prepared had been granted a grace period until March 31, 2027, with full compliance required from April 1 next year.
He also said the amendments to the Act, which took effect on June 1, introduced the reducing balance method and effective interest rate, replacing the flat interest rate and "Rule of 78" method.
"Under this method, interest is calculated based on the current loan balance, making early loan settlement more transparent for consumers," he said.
CONFEST 2026, themed "Suara Kita: Kuasa Kita", is organised by the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living from Sept 17 to 20.
The 2026 National Consumer Day celebration aims to raise public awareness of consumer rights, protection and responsibilities.
The programme brings together consumer advocacy groups, government agencies and non-governmental organisations through a range of activities, including consumer-related competitions, a Fun Walk, a Fun Run and booths hosted by the ministry's agencies and strategic partners.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman raped by neighbour she let into home to repair phone
Article:
TAWAU: A 19-year-old woman was raped by her neighbour, whom she had allowed into her home to help repair her mobile phone.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Rosdi Mat Jusoh said police received a report from the victim, who alleged that she was raped by a suspect known to her at a People's Housing Project here last Tuesday.
Rosdi said the 26-year-old man, who works as a barber, was arrested by a team of police officers from the Tawau district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Division at his home about 10pm on Thursday.
Preliminary investigations found that the incident was believed to have occurred after the victim allowed the suspect into her home to help repair her mobile phone.
"The suspect is then believed to have taken the victim to a room before committing the alleged offence," he said in a statement today.
The suspect has been remanded for seven days until Sept 25.

Title: Police yet to confirm illegal racing caused fatal 15-vehicle crash
Article:
BATU GAJAH: Police have yet to confirm whether a fatal accident involving 12 motorcycles that claimed three lives and injured nine others along Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here today was caused by an illegal street race.
Perak deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Azlin Sadari said this could only be confirmed after police recorded statements from the victims who are currently receiving treatment at hospital.
He said preliminary investigations showed that a separate accident involving a car had occurred earlier at the same location, before the vehicle was hit by a group of motorcyclists due to poor lighting conditions.
"Preliminary investigations showed that a car was involved in an accident, causing the vehicle to remain on the main road.
"Poor lighting conditions are believed to have caused a group of motorcyclists to crash into the car.
"Whether they were racing at the time of the incident, we are unable to confirm yet," he said after launching the Amanita Adopted Park Launching Ceremony and Perak Police Chief's Town Hall Discussion Session here today.
In the accident,
three motorcyclists were killed
while nine others were injured.
Azlin said preliminary investigations confirmed that the group of motorcyclists comprised those aged between 19 and 25.
He said they knew one another and were on their way home after gathering near a convenience store in Meru Raya.
In a related development, Azlin said the Perak Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department had conducted 809 operations this year, including 209 operations around Ipoh, to curb street racing and road hooliganism.
He said the crash site was not, however, identified as a preferred location or "hot spot" for road hooligans.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two religious school students assaulted by seniors after skipping class
Article:
ROMPIN: Two religious school students were assaulted by five senior students at a hostel here on Sept 12, after one of them allegedly skipped a religious class, police said.
Rompin deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohamad Zamri Mohamad Zaber said the two Form Two students were called into a room by their seniors around midnight before being beaten.
"They went to the hostel room, where both victims were beaten by five suspects comprising three Form Five and two Form Four students.
"The attack stemmed from one of the victims skipping a religious class, while the other was claimed to be conspiring with him. The victims suffered injuries to their arms and bodies," he said in a statement today.
Zamri said the victims' parents lodged separate police reports at 1pm on Sept 17, alleging that their children had been beaten by the five male students.
He said police arrested all five suspects for questioning on the same day before releasing them on police bail.
The case is being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting, which carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Earlier, the mother of one of the victims,
Siti Rohani Yusof
, claimed the incident had left her family traumatised after the suspects allegedly hit her son with a broomstick and threatened him with a penknife.
She also claimed the school had been slow to take action, prompting her to lodge a police report and transfer her son out of the school.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka PH, Bersatu in talks to form 'PH Plus' for state election
Article:
MELAKA: State Pakatan Harapan is finalising negotiations with parties that share similar aspirations, including Bersatu, to form a PH Plus collaboration to contest the Melaka election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the negotiations were being conducted based on decisions made at a meeting of the PH Presidential Council.
"The negotiations also include Bersatu, but any form of cooperation will only be announced after the negotiation process has been completed," he told a press conference after attending the launch of Amanah's election machinery in Duyong here today.
Also present were Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who is also agriculture and food security minister, and Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa.
Meanwhile, Adly, who is also deputy defence minister, said the distribution of seats within PH among PKR, Amanah and DAP had been finalised, including the allocation of eight seats to Amanah.
Among the state seats Amanah is set to contest are Bukit Katil, Durian Tunggal, Telok Mas and Merlimau.
Asked about the possibility of collaborating with Barisan Nasional, Adly said no negotiations had been held with the party so far.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MMA calls for tougher enforcement after repeat illegal clinic discoveries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has called for tougher enforcement after the latest discovery of suspected illegal clinics and seizure of unregistered medicines and medical equipment.
"What is particularly worrying is that this comes only months after similar illegal clinics were uncovered earlier this year," MMA president Dr L. Sivanaesan said in a statement.
He said the use of unregistered medicines, injections, antibiotics and medical equipment by unqualified or unregistered individuals posed a serious risk to patients and public health. It said inappropriate use of antibiotics could also contribute to antimicrobial resistance.
Healthcare must be provided by qualified and registered professionals at premises registered with the relevant authorities, using only approved medicines and medical equipment in treating patients, Dr Sivanaesan said.
The association called for tougher, sustained and intelligence-led enforcement, including coordinated inspections of suspected premises and regular follow-up inspections at locations previously found to be operating illegally.
Dr Sivanaesan said enforcement must also follow the supply chain, including how unregistered medicines are brought into the country and those who knowingly facilitate their distribution. It also called for stricter checks at the country's entry points to prevent unregistered medicines from entering Malaysia.
MMA said stronger action was needed not only against those operating illegal clinics, but also against the networks supplying and facilitating the unlawful activities.
Dr Sivanaesan said the government should also address healthcare access challenges faced by undocumented migrants, as fear of coming into contact with enforcement authorities might discourage some from seeking care at registered healthcare facilities, leaving them vulnerable to illegal providers.
MMA urged the public not to compromise their health to save a small amount of money, saying treatment from unqualified individuals or illegal clinics might appear cheaper but could result in serious health and financial consequences.
In June, the Health Ministry said it would step up enforcement against unlicensed healthcare premises, including those offering aesthetic medical services, following a rise in complaints.
The ministry said it had received more than 1,020 complaints about unlicensed medical facilities since 2021, with the number increasing each year.
"The
recurrence raises questions
about whether enforcement is sufficiently sustained to prevent such operations from simply resurfacing elsewhere," Dr Sivanaesan said.

Title: 12,575 still waiting for organ transplants as donor numbers rise
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The Health Ministry recorded 102 deceased organ donors from January to August this year, up from 89 in 2025, but 12,575 patients remain on the waiting list for new organs as of July.
Deputy director-general of health (Medical) Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said the figures, equivalent to about 1.3 deceased donors per million population, showed that public awareness of organ donation had taken root but remained far from satisfactory.
"Compared to international statistics, countries such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Spain and others have higher organ acceptance rates, reaching 20 to 30 per million population," he told reporters after officiating the launch of National Organ Donation Awareness Week (MKPO) 2026 here today.
Speaking on this year's theme, "Warisku, Hormati Ikrarku" (My Heirs, Honour My Pledge), he said MKPO carried the message that a person's wish to donate their organs after death was a humanitarian pledge that deserved to be honoured, with family support and understanding.
Dr Azman said many families were unaware of their loved one's wish to donate, which was among the reasons the number of deceased organ donations remained low and more lives could not be saved.
He said although some 450,000 individuals were registered as organ donors, the number of actual donations remained low as families had the final say on whether donation proceeded after death.
"When the time comes, when a donor falls ill due to an accident, brain death or other causes, they can no longer make the decision. So awareness among family members is crucial to honouring the donor's wishes," he said.
Dr Azman said Terengganu was chosen to host this year's MKPO following encouraging progress in organ and tissue donation across the East Coast states, reflecting growing public awareness.
He said Terengganu recorded seven organ or tissue donation procedures this year, while Pahang and Kelantan each recorded one, their first in a long time.
Meanwhile, Dr Azman said the Health Ministry would continue efforts to increase the number of actual organ donors through various measures.
These include setting up the National Transplant Council as a strategic platform to improve coordination of the country's organ donation and transplantation agenda.
He added that the ministry would also step up engagement with institutions across all religions to help the public better understand organ donation, including the fact that it does not contradict religious requirements.
"Sustained explanation of the legal and religious aspects is crucial, as confusion over these matters can be a factor deterring people from coming forward as organ donors," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: One-off RM1,000 allowance for Perkeso contributors taking jobs over 100km away
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The government will provide a one-off RM1,000 Mobility Assistance Allowance to Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributors who secure new jobs located more than 100km from their homes.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said under the Act the allowance would take effect on Oct 1 through amendments to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017.
Among the changes is an increase in the Early Re-employment Allowance from 25 per cent to 50 per cent of the remaining unpaid Job Search Allowance for eligible workers who return to employment early.
"The daily Training Allowance will increase from between RM10 and RM20 to RM30, while the maximum Training Fee covered will rise from RM4,000 to RM7,000.
"This means contributors will receive better support to undergo training, improve their skills and adapt to current job market requirements," Ramanan said at the launch of the three-day Mega iLINDUNGu Festival: Kesuma Bersama Rakyat at Strand Mall here.
Ramanan said under the Act, support and protection provided under the Employment Insurance System (EIS) for each contributor amounted to up to RM25,000.
"However, this is subject to eligibility and the benefits received," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five students arrested over assault of 14-year-old schoolboy
Article:
KUANTAN: A businesswoman was left distressed after her 14-year-old son was allegedly assaulted by several senior students using a broomstick at a religious secondary school in Rompin last week.
What upset the 40-year-old was the school's alleged failure to look into the matter despite being alerted by her son, prompting her to take matters into her own hands, including lodging a police report and "rescuing" her son from the school.
Siti Rohani Yusof said the incident had left her family traumatised, particularly her son, while the alleged lack of action by the school, including its principal and hostel warden, came as a shock.
The mother of two said the incident occurred on Sept 12, when five senior students called her son and his friend to their hostel room at about midnight before advising them not to leave the school premises without permission.
"Suddenly, they blindfolded my son and began punching him in the stomach, kicking his back, slapping his face and hitting him with a broomstick.
"They assaulted him for more than an hour. They even threatened to injure him with a penknife and a piece of glass," she told reporters at her house in Bukit Rangin here today.
She said her son informed the school management about the incident, but no action was taken.
Upon learning that the senior students were planning another assault, her son called and informed his father using a public phone on Sept 16.
Siti Rohani said when she contacted the hostel warden, she was told there was no need for her to travel to the school as the matter had been settled.
"I decided to immediately go to the school and, upon reaching the hostel, I was shocked to see my son's body and hands covered in bruises.
"The seniors allegedly involved in the incident were moving around freely.
"I lodged a police report on Sept 17 and took my son to hospital for a check-up. When I shared details about the incident with other parents, I was informed that several children had previously been assaulted by the seniors but the incidents were never disclosed by the school," she said.
Siti Rohani said she was upset that the school, despite being aware of the incident involving its students, had allegedly chosen to conceal the matter.
"My son was forced to treat his own injuries... I am fortunate that my son is still alive.
"Concerned about my son's safety, I told him to pack his belongings on Sept 16 and I am in the process of transferring him to another school," she said.
Meanwhile, Rompin deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohamad Zamri Mohamad Zaber said police had arrested five students after two victims lodged separate reports at about 1pm on Sept 17.
He said the suspects, comprising three Form Five and two Form Four students, were questioned to assist investigations under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting.
The offence carries a maximum two years' imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
"Both victims sustained injuries believed to have resulted from the assault. All the suspects have been released on police bail," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM10 per member: Umno sets RM30mil goal to help Najib pay court fine
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno is targeting up to RM30 million for the Tabung Solidariti Najib Razak if all of its estimated 3.8 million members nationwide contribute to the fund.
Umno supreme council member Datuk Razlan Rafii said the target was achievable if each member contributed at least RM10.
"Looking at the amount collected so far, we are positive about the support given to the Tabung Solidariti Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
"After this, contributions will be easier once we obtain the bank's QR code, allowing people to use digital platforms to contribute," he said when contacted today.
Razlan said organisers were optimistic that the target could be reached as soon as possible, with no official closing date set for the fund.
Umno launched the fund to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay a RM50 million fine imposed as a condition of his conditional pardon.
Recalling a similar effort in the past, Razlan said he had previously launched a fund in July 2018 to help pay part of Najib's bail in the case involving alleged misappropriation of SRC International funds.
"Previously, we launched a fund to help with Najib's bail and managed to collect RM500,000 within a short period, thanks to the spirit of party members," he said.
On negative reactions on social media to the latest fund, Razlan claimed the opposition was deliberately generated by certain parties using "cyber armies".
"Many support Najib, but we face challenges when certain parties deliberately campaign to shape public opinion in Malaysia.
"These are all paid bots; it is not a true reflection of Malaysians," he said.
Razlan also urged the public to consider Najib's contributions and services fairly.
"Every leader has their contributions and achievements. The wrongs or mistakes they have made should be balanced against their contributions. That is what is most important," he said.
He also commented on the stance previously taken by some government leaders who had said they were prepared to resign if Najib was granted a pardon.
Razlan said the current situation showed how far the leaders concerned valued their positions over their principles.
"Today, we can see how much they value their positions over their principles," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New MyKad: Dyed hair allowed if not too prominent
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Applicants for the new-generation MyKad are allowed to have dyed hair as long as the colour looks natural and is not too prominent.
National Registration Department Identification Card Division director Muhammad Asraf Sukadi said the requirement also took into account an individual's original hair colour, including those with grey hair or who use henna.
He said the department did not require applicants to have black hair, but the colour should closely resemble their natural hair colour and not be excessive.
"We allow hair colours that are close to the original colour. For example, grey hair or hair coloured using henna, as long as it is not too prominent.
"For example, if someone is of Eurasian descent, we allow it, and there is no problem. But it should not be completely blonde. The colour should be more natural," he said during an interview on a programme with radio station Kool FM.
The clarification followed a picture of a new-generation MyKad belonging to a female singer that went viral on social media, prompting discussion over hair colour and several other requirements for identification card photographs.
Meanwhile, he said claims that applicants must wear a black headscarf when having their photograph taken for the new MyKad were inaccurate.
He said the department required applicants wearing headscarves to use dark colours because the background of the MyKad photograph was white.
"We did not say black. We said dark colours because the background is white.
"If they wear a light-coloured headscarf, we will not be able to see it properly in the photograph," he said
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] DAP leaders arrive for emergency CEC meeting over Najib pardon [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke and other party leaders have arrived at the DAP headquarters here for an emergency central executive committee (CEC) meeting.
The meeting is being held following the latest development involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, who was granted a conditional pardon.
Loke arrived at 2.54pm, followed by other leaders, including DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo and Wanita DAP chief Teo Nie Ching.
Also spotted arriving for the meeting were DAP deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh, who sits on the Federal Territories Pardons Board, and DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming, as well as other party leaders.
It was reported yesterday that Najib was granted house arrest for the remainder of his sentence on condition that he pays the
RM50 million
fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board, in a statement, had said that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed for him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
It also said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RTS Link: Border security preparations stepped up ahead of January launch
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) is stepping up security readiness and border inspection capabilities ahead of the launch of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link in January next year.
MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said preparations were being intensified through technology, personnel training and operational simulations to ensure effective inspection of documents and goods.
He said while technology played an important role in supporting enforcement, it could not be regarded as the sole solution to security threats at the country's entry points.
"Technology helps, but it is not the solution to these threats. A combination of both is essential, while how we utilise technology for enforcement is equally important, including training," he told Bernama recently.
Shuhaily said MCBA would also advise operators on suitable technologies to enhance security and mitigate potential risks.
On the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help curb the smuggling of illicit goods, he said the technology needed to undergo a learning phase, including machine learning, before reaching maturity.
"Before AI can mature, it needs to learn through what is known as machine learning. So, it is still a work in progress," he said.
Meanwhile, Shuhaily said 400 MCBA trainees were undergoing a three-month training programme at the Segamat Police Training Centre ahead of their deployment to the RTS Link.
He said the trainees were expected to complete their training by the end of September before being deployed to the RTS Link in October.
"We will conduct dry runs over the remaining two months so that by January, everyone is fully prepared to operate this new facility," he said.
Shuhaily said the personnel would initially work alongside senior officers at the Sultan Iskandar Building to gain experience, particularly in inspecting documents and goods.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC chief says media key to anti-corruption efforts
Article:
KAJANG: The media plays a key role in helping the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) combat corruption by delivering accurate and responsible information to the public, its chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said.
He said the commission could not fight corruption alone and regarded the media as one of its key strategic partners.
"In today's fast-moving digital era, the public not only needs information quickly, but, more importantly, they need information that is authentic, truthful, accurate and responsible.
"I sincerely hope the good relationship between the MACC and the media can continue to be strengthened, particularly in ensuring that corruption-related issues are reported professionally, ethically and with integrity," he said.
Abd Halim was speaking at the MACC Shooting Programme with the Media at Kajang Prison College here today.
Also present were MACC Strategic Communications Division director Hisyam Mohd Yusoff, MACC Intelligence Division senior director Datuk Saiful Ezral Arifin, Media Prima Bhd News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim and New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd chief operating officer Luqman Adrine Ja'afar.
Abd Halim said integrity was fundamental to maintaining public trust in journalism, as every report could affect public perception and the reputation of individuals and organisations.
He said news reports could also influence public confidence in the country's institutions.
The MACC remained committed to ensuring information on its enforcement actions and anti-corruption efforts was properly communicated to the public, he said.
Abd Halim said that the fight against corruption went beyond arrests, prosecutions and punishment.
"It is also about prevention, education, awareness and cultivating integrity as a value in our daily lives.
"In this regard, our media partners have a very important role in conveying that message to the people," he said.
Abd Halim expressed hope that engagement programmes with the media would continue and become part of ongoing efforts to strengthen ties between the commission and journalists.
He said the shooting programme also gave media practitioners an opportunity to experience, albeit on a different scale, the level of precision, discipline, focus, emotional control and accuracy required of MACC officers in carrying out their duties.
"When in the field, MACC officers must remain calm and disciplined and exercise sound judgment.
"The use of firearms is not merely about strength or courage. It requires discipline, self-control, compliance with safety procedures and a high degree of responsibility," he said.
Hafidzul Hilmi Mohd Noor, representing Harian Metro, took third place, while Sinar Harian's Muhammad Afham Ramli took second place in the men's centre-fire category.
Meanwhile, Nur Ayuni Johari from Malaysia Gazette took first place in the women's centre-fire category.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australian man pleads not guilty to Thai suitcase murder
Article:
BANGKOK: An Australian accused of murdering a teenage girl in Thailand and abandoning her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty in court on Friday, citing self-defence.
Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested at a Bangkok airport in June as he prepared to take a flight back to Australia, after the 17-year-old victim's friend had reported her missing.
The young woman's body was found in a suitcase near a railway track in Pattaya, a seaside resort city south of the capital Bangkok.
Police said she died of suffocation.
Carman appeared on Friday at Pattaya Provincial Court, where he denied all charges, citing "self-defence and a mistaken belief about the victim's age", a court statement said. It did not elaborate further.
The Australian is charged with murder, concealing a body and taking a minor aged between 15 and 18 for indecent purposes.
The court denied Carman's bail application after prosecutors opposed his release, saying he posed a flight risk. The next court date was set for October 12.
Police previously said CCTV footage showed him entering a condominium in Pattaya with the girl and leaving that evening carrying a large black suitcase.
The case put the spotlight on Pattaya, which is popular with foreign tourists for its beaches and nightlife, but also has a reputation for sex tourism.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 68,177 people lost jobs between January and Sept 16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 68,177 workers lost their jobs between January and Sept 16 this year, an increase of 15,196 from the same period last year.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said workers in the manufacturing and wholesale and retail sectors were among those most affected.
He said although the figure showed an increase, the labour market remained resilient overall, with the labour force and number of employed people continuing to grow as of July this year.
"As of July, the labour force had increased to 17.37 million, while the number of employed people reached 16.85 million, with the labour force participation rate remaining at 70.9 per cent.
"The unemployment rate remained at three per cent, the same as the previous month, involving about 520,300 unemployed people," he said during the Global Supply Crisis Briefing here today.
Akmal said the situation showed that the country's labour market remained stable overall, although certain sectors continued to face pressure.
He said the government remained vigilant about the development, particularly the increase in job losses in affected sectors.
He said the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) had also implemented job placement initiatives through the Employment Insurance System (EIS) and MYFutureJobs portal to help workers who had lost their jobs return to the labour market.
From January to Sept 11, he said 143,653 workers had secured new jobs through the initiatives.
"The development shows that government intervention is not merely about providing temporary support to affected workers, but also helping them secure new employment and return to work.
"It also reflects that although the labour market remains stable overall, continued attention is needed to address job losses occurring in certain sectors," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Workers to get enhanced EIS benefits, training support from October
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Workers will receive enhanced financial and training support from October, with the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) also expanding employment opportunities and social protection initiatives under a broader effort to strengthen Malaysia's workforce safety net.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said amendments to the Employment Insurance System (EIS) Act, passed by the Dewan Rakyat last December, would improve benefits for contributors who lose their jobs and strengthen the system's governance.
Among the changes is an increase in the Early Re-employment Allowance from 25 per cent to 50 per cent of the remaining unpaid Job Search Allowance for eligible workers who return to employment early.
The daily training allowance will increase from between RM10 and RM20 to RM30, while the maximum training fee covered will rise from RM4,000 to RM7,000.
Eligible contributors who secure employment more than 100km from their homes will also receive a new one-off Mobility Assistance Allowance of RM1,000.
The amendments also strengthen Perkeso's role in providing employment services, including job matching, career counselling and other active labour market programmes.
"People who come here should not leave with just information. We want them to go home with employment opportunities, access to social protection and solutions.
"For those looking for a job or seeking to advance their careers, seize this opportunity. We are bringing employers and job opportunities directly to the people," Ramanan said at the launch of the three-day Festival Mega iLindungu: Kesuma Bersama Rakyat at Strand Mall here.
The festival, which runs until tomorrow, features the Lindung Kerjaya Carnival by MyFutureJobs, with 25 employers offering more than 2,000 vacancies with salaries ranging from RM2,000 to RM12,000.
Job seekers can also obtain resume guidance and job-matching services, while visitors can access free health screenings, contribution checks, benefits advice and registration for Perkeso schemes.
The event also saw gig economy platforms Grab, Foodpanda and Haloje Delivery pledge RM1,514,412.40 in Perkeso contributions, expected to benefit about 500 e-hailing and p-hailing riders.
Ramanan said the initiative was important as gig workers and their families needed protection against unexpected risks.
"Behind every rider and driver, there is a family that depends on their income.
"That is why social protection is not something to be taken lightly. It is a vital safety net when something unexpected happens," he said.
Meanwhile, 400 housewives from the Sungai Buloh parliamentary constituency received RM48,000 under the Lindung Kasih Suri Rumah initiative at the event.
The festival brings together Perkeso and 11 agencies under the Human Resources Ministry, offering visitors access to employment, skills development, social protection and other services in one location.
About 60,000 visitors are expected to attend the three-day event, which runs from 10am to 10pm daily.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Indonesia accepts Malaysia's offer to help tackle forest fires
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia has accepted Malaysia's offer to help tackle forest fires in the republic that have led to weeks of haze.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto had given the green light to Malaysia's offer to help put out forest fires in Kalimantan, where more than 1,400 hotspots have been detected.
"We've also agreed to longer-term planning to prevent a recurrence of the haze from forest fires, which are also happening in Sumatera and other regions in Indonesia," Zahid told a press conference here.
Zahid said Prabowo informed him that action had been
taken against 95 companies
involved in open burning in Kalimantan.
"Malaysia welcomes the measures taken to extinguish the fires and we too will help them because it affects Sarawak.
"I have told Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan to coordinate Malaysia's assistance in firefighting efforts."
He said the Malaysian authorities involved include the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Fire and Rescue Department, the Malaysian Army, the Malaysia Civil Defence Force and the Malaysian Meteorological Department, which typically handles cloud seeding.
Separately,
Zahid said Indonesia
was looking into the possible involvement of Malaysian companies in the fires, although he had so far not received any information.
"Perhaps in terms of shareholding, there may be a small number of companies owned by Malaysian shareholders."
Last week, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he discussed the haze issue with Prabowo on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, India.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH Presidential Council discussed house arrest, not GE16, says Mat Sabu
Article:
MELAKA: The Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council meeting yesterday focused on the legal and procedural aspects of implementing house arrest, says Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said house arrest was a new concept in Malaysia and its implementation needed to be carefully studied from legal and operational perspectives.
Mohamad said matters concerning its implementation had been left to the relevant authorities, particularly the Attorney-General, to examine the necessary procedures and standard operating procedures (SOP).
The meeting followed the Pardons Board's decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak house arrest for the remainder of his sentence, on condition that he pays the RM50 million fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/1535336/najib-granted-house-arrest-remainder-sentence-subject-rm50m-fine-watch
The Pardons Board also said Najib must comply with all conditions imposed for him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
"The general election was not discussed at yesterday's PH Presidential Council meeting. What was discussed was how to handle this new situation regarding house arrest," said Mohamad, who is commonly known as Mat Sabu.
"This is something new in Malaysia. In terms of the law and other aspects, it will be studied," he said after launching the Melaka Amanah election machinery in Duyong.
Asked about the timing of the next general election, Mohamad said the decision rested with the prime minister, although he hoped it would be held towards the end of next year.
"For the prime minister, it can be anytime he deems suitable. It is his right to decide," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia to study proposal for India's BrahMos missile system
Article:
LUMUT: Malaysia will study a proposal to acquire India's BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
"Whatever it is, we will study it for each service. If this is for air-to-surface missiles, it comes under the Air Force, so we will study it," he said.
He said the proposal, which was raised during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's recent visit to India, would first be studied by the Royal Malaysian Air Force.
"Whenever not only the prime minister, but ministers as well, travel anywhere, there are many parties wanting to
sell
all kinds of things," he said.
He told reporters this after opening the 93rd Armed Forces Day celebrations at the Royal Malaysian Navy Base here today.
He said the assessment would also consider the implications of integrating the proposed missile system with existing equipment, including whether upgrades would be required for the Sukhoi fighter jets.
"We also have to look at our defence doctrine," he said.
Khaled said Malaysia's existing missiles had a range of slightly more than 100km, while the proposed system had a range of between 300km and 400km.
"So, who are we going to fire at? That depends on our defence doctrine," he said.
The BrahMos system is a long-range, ramjet-powered supersonic cruise missile jointly developed by India's Defence Research and Development Organisation and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya through their joint venture, BrahMos Aerospace.
The missile can be deployed from multiple platforms, including land-based mobile launchers, warships, submarines and fighter aircraft, giving operators flexibility in conducting precision strikes against targets at sea and on land.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH will contest Melaka election regardless of cooperation outcome, says Fuziah
Article:
KUANTAN: There has yet to be any decision on potential political cooperation for the Melaka election, but Pakatan Harapan (PH) will contest the polls regardless of the outcome.
PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the coalition was ready to enter the election battleground and face its opponents in the Melaka state election.
"No decision has been made regarding political cooperation for the Melaka state election, but the fight goes on.
"Whatever the outcome, we are prepared to contest in Melaka," she told reporters after opening the Madani Kita programme at Dewan Serbaguna Sungai Isap Damai here today.
She was commenting on talks over possible political cooperation with Barisan Nasional to contest the Melaka election.
On rumours that PH would cooperate with Bersatu in the Melaka election, Fuziah said there had been no official decision or announcement on the matter.
Meanwhile, Fuziah reiterated that PH would continue its fight against corruption and would not tolerate any form of misconduct or abuse involving corrupt practices.
"PH would not accept any situation involving corruption, abuse of power or misappropriation, and would remain committed to ensuring that such wrongdoing is looked into.
"The PH Presidential Council remains firmly behind Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Attorney-General Tan Sri Dusuki Mokhtar and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh,
that no one is above the law
and the Constitution is supreme," she said.
She was commenting on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional house arrest order, which allows him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to a RM50 million fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brazil police nab suspected serial killer disguised as woman
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazilian police said Friday they had captured a suspected serial killer linked to at least 16 deaths since May, who was arrested while disguised as a woman and carrying a baby.
He claims to have killed more than four times that number.
The suspect was arrested Sunday after a 30-hour police manhunt in a forested area of Paraiba state in northeastern Brazil.
He was wearing a dress and long black wig, which police described as a disguise to evade capture. In a statement, they said he had been carrying a baby in his arms.
Local media reported the child was not related to the suspect. Police did not release details on the baby's condition or say where it came from.
"Although the suspect claimed involvement in 80 homicides, civil police have confirmed his participation in 16 killings in the region, 11 of which he confessed to during questioning," police told AFP.
The 16 homicides all took place since May. The identities of the victims and details of the killings have not been made public.
The suspect evaded an earlier attempt to arrest him a few weeks ago after a confrontation with security forces, who consider him a member of an "ultra-violent" criminal group.
In a video of his interrogation obtained by AFP, the man said he acted alone and denied having ties to organised crime.
Instead, he claimed that all his victims were "linked to the criminal world" and that he was taking justice into his own hands in response to threats against himself and his family.
"I never acted against any family man, mother or working person," he said, denying being a "psychopath."
He said he had committed his first homicide at the age of 13.
After the earlier attempt to arrest the suspect, police seized bulletproof vests, the stock of a submachine gun, and over 100 rounds of ammunition, which the man acknowledged were his during questioning.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bukit Aman’s USJT takes over probe into viral theatre clip mocking Rukun Negara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The Classified Criminal Investigation Unit (USJT) of the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has taken over the investigation into a viral theatre performance video that allegedly mocks the five principles of the Rukun Negara and contains racially sensitive remarks.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed that the report on the case was lodged at the Jalan Tun Razak Police Station under the Wangsa Maju District Police Headquarters (IPD) at 8.30pm yesterday.
He said a complainant lodged the report after spotting a stage performance video clip uploaded by the Instagram account @THEFEVERKINETIC. The clip was believed to have been deleted before a Facebook user re-shared it.
“The investigation into this case will be fully conducted by Bukit Aman's USJT. We expect several more police reports on the same issue to be lodged nationwide, and all will be referred to the initial report in Wangsa Maju,” he said when contacted today.
The 10-minute video clip features five actors reciting each principle of the Rukun Negara, with statements that could be considered racially sensitive.
Police said an initial review found the video's content could cause public concern and affect social harmony.
Checks revealed that The Fever Kinetic is an intercultural physical theatre group founded by a local choreographer, with bases in Malaysia and London, United Kingdom.
The clip is believed to be a recording of a theatre performance staged during the Theatre for The Arts event in 2018. The group re-uploaded it for the recent Malaysia Day celebrations. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar flags off Malaysia Sarong Music Run 2026 at Twin Towers, joins three‑kilometre walk
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today flagged off the Malaysia Sarong Music Run 2026 in front of the Petronas Twin Towers here.
Speaking at the event, Anwar thanked participants of all ages and backgrounds for joining the run and helping promote healthy living in the community.
“Women and men are committed to staying fit, looking after our health and taking care of our beloved Malaysia. Come on, let’s run together in our sarongs!” he said briefly before flagging off the event.
Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing.
Dressed in sportswear and wearing a sarong sash, Anwar later joined participants on a three-kilometre walk.
Now in its third year, the Malaysia Sarong Music Run celebrates culture, heritage and an active lifestyle, with cultural elements incorporated along the route to give participants a deeper experience of Malaysia’s traditions. — Bernama

Title: Police yet to confirm if Ipoh pre-dawn crash involving 15 vehicles linked to illegal racing
Article:
BATU GAJAH, Sept 19 — Police have yet to confirm whether a group of motorcyclists involved in a fatal accident involving 12 motorcycles and three cars at Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here early today were linked to illegal racing.
Perak deputy police chief DCP Mohammad Azlin Sadari said police needed to record statements from nine injured motorcyclists still receiving treatment in hospital to determine what happened before and during the crash.
He said the riders, aged between 19 and 25, were travelling together from Meru Jaya before the accident.
“Police are also investigating the possibility that poor lighting conditions at the location contributed to the crash,” he told reporters after the Taman Angkat Amanita launch and a town hall discussion here today.
In the 3.35am incident, two motorcyclists aged 19 and 20 died at the scene, while another 19-year-old rider died while receiving treatment at Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital (HRPB).
Mohammad Azlin said initial investigations found a car accident had occurred earlier at the location, causing the vehicle involved to be positioned in the path of other road users.
The group of motorcyclists, travelling close together, then collided with the vehicle, resulting in a chain collision.
Meanwhile, Mohammad Azlin said dashcam footage had helped police identify two men suspected of threatening a driver with a stick along Jalan Ipoh-Gopeng, Simpang Pulai here.
He said police were waiting for the appropriate time to call the two local men to record their statements.
Mohammad Azlin said no serious incident occurred apart from a verbal altercation before both parties left the scene. A police report has been lodged, and the case is being investigated under Section 506 of the Penal Code.
A one-minute-30-second video of the incident had earlier gone viral on Threads.
Earlier, Mohammad Azlin said three areas under the Batu Gajah District Police Headquarters - Kampung Ara Payung, Taman Batu Gajah Perdana and Taman Tasek Putra, Tronoh, had been selected as Amanita Adopted Neighbourhoods for 2026.
He said the initiative aims to involve women, particularly housewives, as strategic partners in raising crime awareness and promoting prevention efforts within their communities.
Through Amanita, PDRM can better understand residents’ safety concerns while providing a closer channel for the public to share information and report suspicious activities or criminal incidents.
He added that the programme also strengthens two-way communication between police and the community to address local safety issues. — Bernama

Title: Loke to resign as Transport Minister, DAP stays in Anwar’s government after Najib’s conditional pardon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Anthony Loke Siew Fook will step down from his position as Transport Minister in the Pakatan Harapan-led unity government following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
He said DAP will remain in the federal unity government, with its ministers continuing to serve in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s Cabinet.
“We respect the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s pardoning powers but as a party, DAP has its own stance on this matter (Najib’s conditional pardon) and we feel this is something that is hard for Malaysians to accept.
“So, after discussing what the party’s response should be for almost three hours, I have offered to resign as Transport Minister,” Loke told reporters after chairing DAP’s central executive committee (CEC) meeting at the party headquarters in Pudu today.
“The resignation will only involve me, while the other Cabinet members from DAP will continue in the government,” he added.
Loke said his colleagues were also willing to resign from their respective positions at any given time but stressed that DAP’s backing for Anwar’s unity government was crucial to prevent attempts to topple the federal government.
Loke added that he would submit his resignation letter to Anwar soon. However, he will stay on as DAP’s secretary-general and as the Seremban MP.
When asked about the Transport Ministry’s operations after his resignation, Loke said: “Ministers come and go. Of course, I will require some time because there are some outstanding work.
“I’ll discuss with the Prime Minister but it won’t be long. The projects that have been approved will go on,” he added.
DAP came under heavy pressure from party grassroots and supporters after His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, consented to a conditional pardon for Najib yesterday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his jail term under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
The conditional pardon, however, is subject to Najib settling his RM50 million fine.
Najib has been serving his 12-year jail term at Kajang Prison following his conviction in the SRC International case in August 2022.
His jail term was subsequently halved to six years and his fine was reduced from RM210 million to RM50 million by the Pardons Board in 2024.

Title: Air quality dips nationwide, Sarawak records seven unhealthy API readings, Klang Valley four, Johor three
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — A total of 17 areas nationwide recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4 pm today.
According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Sarawak recorded seven areas with unhealthy readings, namely IPD Serian (178), Kuching (171), Sri Aman (168), Samarahan (164), Sibu (157), Sarikei (152) and Bintulu (106).
In Johor, three areas recorded unhealthy readings, namely Larkin (158), Pasir Gudang (155) and Tangkak (102), followed by Kuala Lumpur with Cheras (149) and Batu Muda (121).
Seri Manjung in Perak recorded a reading of 159, while Shah Alam in Selangor recorded 152.
Putrajaya (121), Nilai in Negeri Sembilan (111) and Bukit Rambai in Melaka (108) were also at unhealthy levels.
Meanwhile, 38 other areas recorded moderate readings, while 12 areas recorded good air quality.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Police probe Rompin religious school hostel assault, five senior students freed on bail
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 19 — A mother has claimed that her 14-year-old son and another Form Two student were assaulted by five students at a religious school hostel in Bukit Ibam, Rompin, resulting in injuries to various parts of their bodies.
Siti Rohani Yusof, 40, said the first incident occurred at about midnight on Sept 12 when the two students were called into a hostel room, had their heads covered and were allegedly beaten, with her son assaulted for about two hours and his friend for about two and a half hours.
“My son did not dare to tell anyone after the incident for fear of being beaten again. Only on Tuesday did he inform the warden and teachers about what happened.
“He also pleaded to sleep at the warden’s house as he was afraid the incident would recur, but was not allowed to,” she said when met here today.
She said her son was allegedly assaulted again on Sept 15 by the same students using a broomstick, with one holding the stick while another kicked him.
She said her son then contacted his father, who informed the warden, before she went to the school the following day.
She said the senior students allegedly kicked, pinched, slapped and punched her son, besides hitting him with a broomstick.
Her son was later taken to Muadzam Shah Hospital for a medical examination, including X-rays, after a police report was lodged at the Muadzam Shah Police Station.
Siti Rohani said she had also requested police to investigate the hostel management, including the school and warden’s actions in handling the incident.
“I want this matter to be investigated transparently and for the relevant authorities to take the initiative to prevent such incidents from happening again, as well as ensuring the safety and welfare of students in the hostel are guaranteed,” she said.
She also claimed that after the matter was shared in the school’s boys’ hostel (Aspura) parents’ group, more students came forward to share their experiences, and she understood that about 16 students had been victims of similar incidents.
Siti Rohani said she had decided to transfer her son to another school due to concerns over his safety.
Meanwhile, Rompin police chief Supt Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi confirmed that police had received a report regarding a fight involving two Form Two students at a boys’ hostel of a religious school in Bukit Ibam.
He said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred at about 12.01 am on Sept 12 after both victims were called to a hostel room by five male students, comprising three Form Five students and two Form Four students.
“The cause of the incident was that the first victim skipped religious lectures, while the second victim was complicit with the first. Both victims were beaten by all the suspects,” he said in a statement today.
Sharif Shai said the first victim suffered injuries to both arms, while the second victim sustained injuries to his body.
He added that all five suspects were detained before being released on police bail, with the case being investigated under Section 147 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak, Penang to get greater focus in Malaysia fertility push, says women’s minister
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 19 — Sarawak and Penang will receive greater focus under the government’s efforts to improve Malaysia’s fertility rate and address the country’s low birth rate, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said the ministry planned to place greater emphasis on fertility-related programmes next year, including measures to support couples facing difficulties conceiving.
“Fertility programmes are important because our population is still low and we want to increase it. So we have also proposed programmes related to fertility.
“Sarawak and Penang are among the states that need to be given focus because we want to increase the birth rate,” she told reporters after launching the
Program Perantisan Kepimpinan Wanita
(Perantis) —
Program Pembinaan Kepimpinan dan Keusahawanan Wanita Dayak
(Pendaya) 2.0 initiative at Dayak Chamber Tower here today.
Nancy said the ministry’s efforts would include programmes to assist couples facing difficulties having children, including initiatives under the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), such as in-vitro fertilisation (IVF).
She said while such programmes were already being implemented, the ministry intended to give them greater emphasis next year as part of efforts to encourage more young people to have children.
“For us, our focus is more on programmes that can encourage them to have children. Our population needs to increase in this country,” she said.
Nancy said proposals for fertility-related programmes had been included in the ministry’s budget submission, although the final allocation would depend on approval.
She added that studies had also been conducted on fertility rates to support efforts to formulate measures to increase birth rates in Malaysia.
However, she said the figures and findings from the studies would be shared at a later date. — The Borneo Post

Title: Najib’s conditional pardon has not strained unity government, says DPM Zahid
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Relations among the parties that make up the unity government remain good following the Pardons Board’s decision involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said that in managing government affairs, all parties continue to act professionally, with Cabinet decisions being made collectively.
“The relationship remains good and, although we are politicians, when it comes to managing government affairs, we act professionally, and there is no problem because all decisions by the Cabinet are made collectively.
“In terms of personal relations, Alhamdulillah, they remain good so far. As members of the unity government, we will continue to uphold the principles of discipline as long as we are in the unity government,” he told a media conference today.
Yesterday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
The Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department said the order was decided at the 64th Meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya held at Istana Negara.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said the decision of the Pardons Board regarding Najib, which received the consent of His Majesty, was bound by provisions of the Federal Constitution.
“What was decided by the Pardons Board, and received the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, is a decision bound by several clauses in the Malaysian Constitution, and His Majesty would certainly have taken into consideration that legal provisions serve as the basis for the pardon decision.
“So, if any party disputes the King’s decision, it means that it is not in line with the provisions enshrined in the Constitution. Umno and BN themselves are of the view that the law must be obeyed. That position is clear, as reflected in statements I made previously,” he added. — Bernama

Title: DAP leaders gather for emergency CEC meeting over Najib’s conditional pardon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — DAP central executive committee (CEC) members gathered at the party’s national headquarters in Pudu this afternoon for an emergency meeting following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
The meeting, which will determine the party’s official position and next steps following yesterday’s decision, began at 3.30pm.
DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo was among the earliest to arrive, at 2.40pm, followed by secretary-general Anthony Loke at around 3pm.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke arrives at DAP headquarters in Kuala Lumpur September 19, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Other prominent party leaders attending the meeting include Teo Nie Ching, a national vice-chairman and DAP Women’s chief; national deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming; party adviser Lim Guan Eng; national treasurer Ngeh Koo Ham; and Hannah Yeoh.
Last night, Loke said the CEC would determine the party’s official response to the conditional pardon granted to Najib.
