DAP national deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming arrives at DAP headquarters in Kuala Lumpur September 19, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
The Pardons Board announced yesterday that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to allow Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
The emergency meeting comes just over a month after DAP delegates voted at the party’s August 16 conference to remain in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s unity government until the end of the current parliamentary term.
Hannah Yeoh arrives at DAP headquarters in Kuala Lumpur September 19, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
A total of 1,857 delegates, or about 88 per cent of those who cast valid votes, backed remaining in the government, while 242 voted to leave.
DAP has been a longstanding political ally of Anwar and was a key component of the Pakatan Rakyat coalition before becoming part of its successor, Pakatan Harapan.

Title: Fourteen of 20 banks now offer reducing balance hire-purchase financing, says Armizan
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — Fourteen of the 20 banking institutions providing hire-purchase financing had begun offering customers the reducing balance method as of Sept 18, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the remaining six banking institutions are expected to complete the transition to the new method by December 31 at the latest, following engagement sessions with the banks.
“In total, there are 429 entities, comprising banking institutions and hire-purchase providers, registered with the Association of Hire Purchase Companies Malaysia (AHPCM),” he told reporters at the closing ceremony of the Consumer Festival (CONFEST) 2026 at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Armizan added that the ministry had set a target for 80 per cent of hire-purchase providers to offer financing in compliance with the Hire-Purchase (Amendment) Act 2026 by the end of this year.
He noted that hire-purchase providers that are not yet fully prepared have been granted a grace period until March 31, 2027, with full compliance required from April 1 next year.
According to Armizan, the amendments to the Act that took effect on June 1 introduced the reducing balance method and effective interest rate, replacing the flat interest rate and “Rule of 78” method.
“Under this method, interest is calculated based on the current loan balance, making early loan settlement more transparent for consumers,” he said.
CONFEST 2026, themed “
Suara Kita: Kuasa Kita
”, is organised by the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) from Sept 17 to 20.
The 2026 National Consumer Day celebration aims to raise public awareness of consumer rights, protection and responsibilities.
The programme brings together consumer advocacy groups, government agencies and non-governmental organisations through a range of activities, including consumer-related competitions, a Fun Walk, a Fun Run and booths hosted by KPDN agencies and strategic partners. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia aims to finalise new e-commerce Bill this year, says domestic trade minister
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — The government aims to finalise the drafting of a new e-commerce Bill this year, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the ministry had approved the policy decision to repeal the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 and replace it with a new, more comprehensive law.
However, he said the process would require coordination between ministries as well as extensive engagement with stakeholders, including e-commerce platforms, service providers and industry players.
“We know that e-commerce is a broad and comprehensive area, so it requires extensive engagement with stakeholders. We need to examine the matter thoroughly, and I hope it can be finalised,” he told reporters after launching the 2026 Consumer Festival (Confest 2026) at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Armizan said two committees had also been established to expedite the drafting of the bill, including to facilitate coordination between the ministry, the Ministry of Communications and the Ministry of Digital.
He said matters currently being fine-tuned included the division of responsibilities among the ministries and relevant agencies, as well as the regulatory mechanisms for e-commerce platforms.
The next stage would also require a regulatory impact assessment (RIA) in collaboration with the Malaysia Productivity Corporation (MPC) before the bill is submitted for further consideration.
Among the proposals being studied is the introduction of a licensing regime for e-commerce platforms, particularly in view of the influx of goods from overseas, consumer safety and the sustainability of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
However, Armizan said regulation must be balanced so as not to hamper the growth of the e-commerce sector, which provides convenience to consumers and serves as a source of income for traders.
“We want more comprehensive and conducive regulation, but at the same time, we do not want to hamper the growth of e-commerce,” he said.
The government had previously expressed its intention to expedite the drafting of the e-commerce Bill to strengthen the regulation and accountability of platforms, sellers and consumers, given that the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 does not provide a comprehensive legal framework to regulate various aspects of e-commerce. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia records 102 deceased organ donors so far in 2026, but 12,575 still await transplants, says MOH
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 19 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) recorded 102 deceased organ donors from January to August this year.
Deputy Director-General of Health (Medical) Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said this is an increase from the 89 deceased organ donors in 2025, equivalent to roughly 1.3 donors per million population.
He said both figures showed that public awareness of the importance of organ donation had taken root, but was still far from satisfactory, with 12,575 patients still on the waiting list for new organs as of July this year.
“Compared to international statistics, countries such as the UAE (United Arab Emirates), Spain and others have higher organ acceptance rates, reaching 20 to 30 per cent per million population,” he told reporters after officiating the launch of National Organ Donation Awareness Week (MKPO) 2026 here today.
Speaking on this year’s theme, “
Warisku, Hormati Ikrarku
” (My Heirs, Honour My Pledge), he said MKPO carries the message that a person’s wish to donate organs after death is a humanitarian pledge that deserves to be honoured and affirmed through their family’s support and understanding.
Dr Azman said many families are unaware of their loved one’s wish to donate, which is among the reasons deceased organ donation numbers remain low, and why more lives are not being saved.
He noted that although some 450,000 individuals are registered as organ donors, the number of actual donations remains low, since families have the final say on whether donation proceeds after death.
“When the time comes, when a donor falls ill due to an accident, brain death or other causes, they can no longer make the decision. So awareness among family members is crucial to honouring the donor’s wishes,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dr Azman said Terengganu was chosen to host this year’s MKPO in light of encouraging progress in organ and tissue donation across the East Coast states, reflecting growing public awareness.
He said Terengganu recorded seven organ or tissue donation procedures this year, while Pahang and Kelantan each recorded one, their first in a long time.
Meanwhile, Dr Azman said the Health Ministry will continue to work on increasing the number of actual organ donors through various measures.
This includes setting up the National Transplant Council as a strategic platform to drive better coordination of the country’s organ donation and transplantation agenda.
He added that MOH will also step up engagement with institutions across all religions, helping the public better understand organ donation, including the fact that it does not contradict religious requirements.
“Sustained explanation of the legal and religious aspects is crucial, as confusion over these matters can be a factor deterring people from coming forward as organ donors,” he said. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid: Malaysia gets Indonesia’s green light to help battle Kalimantan fires behind haze
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Indonesia has given the green light for Malaysia to assist in tackling forest and land fires in Kalimantan that have caused transboundary haze affecting neighbouring countries, including Malaysia.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto gave his approval during their meeting at Istana Hambalang in conjunction with his working visit to Jakarta.
“President Prabowo welcomed the offer, meaning he has given approval for Malaysia to join efforts to address the haze and fires in Kalimantan,” he told a press conference here today.
The assistance includes a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters, and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (APMM), and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).
Ahmad Zahid, also chairman of the Central Disaster Management Committee, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan was tasked with coordinating assistance with NADMA, APMM, the Malaysian Meteorological Department, RMAF, the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), and other relevant agencies.
“Now that approval has been obtained from President Prabowo, coordination at the ministry, department and agency levels must take place. I hope the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in carrying out this coordination, will ensure that all parties involved in the operation work in a coordinated manner,” he said.
He said the assistance was not merely a short-term measure to put out the fires, as both countries had also discussed and agreed on longer-term measures to prevent haze caused by such fires from recurring.
Ahmad Zahid said Prabowo also informed him during the meeting that there were still 1,426 hotspots in Kalimantan, while the Indonesian government had taken legal action against 95 companies involved in open burning in the Borneo region.
Asked whether any Malaysian companies were among the 95 companies, Ahmad Zahid said no such information had been provided so far, adding that the Indonesian authorities were looking into possible Malaysian involvement.
“The companies are registered as Indonesian companies. In terms of shareholding, however, some of them may have a small proportion of shares owned by Malaysian shareholders,” he said.
He said Malaysia welcomed the measures taken by Indonesia and, as its closest neighbour, would continue to cooperate in tackling fires and transboundary haze, particularly their impact on Sarawak. — Bernama

Title: Defence Ministry shortlists three missile systems for LCS, says Khaled
Article:
LUMUT, Sept 19 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) is in the final stage of shortlisting a surface-to-surface missile system from three countries to replace the system for the Royal Malaysian Navy Littoral Combat Ships (LCS).
Without disclosing the three countries, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said several issues needed to be finalised before a government decision could be made.
“We are at the final stage. We have shortlisted three surface-to-surface missiles from three countries,” he said at a press conference after officiating the launch of the Cyber Force Nucleus Team in conjunction with the 93rd Malaysian Armed Forces Day at the Royal Malaysian Navy Base here today.
In July, Malaysia decided to immediately halt any procurement of new defence equipment or assets from Norway following the country’s decision to revoke the export licence for the LCS missile system.
Meanwhile, commenting on the possibility of Malaysia acquiring the BrahMos air-to-surface missile system from India, he said the matter would be referred to the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) for study.
“If there is a proposal, we will refer it to the RMAF for study, including the implications and integration of the system, as well as upgrading the systems on RMAF defence assets, including the Sukhoi fighter aircraft.
“We will also look at our defence doctrine, because what we currently have has a range of no more than 100 kilometres, while that system has a range of 300 to 400 kilometres,” he said.
Last week, during his visit to New Delhi, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that Malaysia was exploring and studying preliminary discussions on acquiring the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system from India. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution says Home Ministry awaits Pardons Board letter, no Najib house arrest notification yet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The Home Ministry is still waiting for the official written notification of the Pardons Board’s reported decision to place former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak under house arrest before deciding on its next course of action.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry and Prisons Department had yet to receive the letter from the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department, which serves as the secretariat to the Pardons Board.
“Once we receive the notification, only then will we be clear about what further action we need to take, and the steps towards implementing the decision in accordance with the existing provisions of the law.
“As of now, we have not received anything,” he told reporters in Kulim, Kedah today.
He was visiting the families of four young boys who drowned in Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan after trying to retrieve a ball.
Saifuddin said the letter would also clarify whether the Pardons Board had specified the premises where Najib would serve his reported house arrest, or whether the matter had been left to the Prisons Department.
“I need to see the letter first. Currently, Datuk Seri Najib is serving his prison sentence. House arrest means he will not be in prison but at another premises, and there are naturally processes to follow. That is why I said I want to see the letter first,” he said.
He said the ministry would also examine whether the Pardons Board’s decision contained any further instructions or delegated authority to the Prisons Department.
“Based on that letter, we will see whether it is limited to the decision of the Pardons Board, or whether the Board has also given further authority to the Prisons Department. We will examine all of that,” he said.
Saifuddin said Najib was currently still serving his prison sentence, adding that house arrest would mean he was no longer held in prison but instead serve his sentence at another premises, subject to the relevant procedures.
He also referred to the Pardons Board’s previous decision to reduce Najib’s 12-year prison sentence to six years and his RM210 million fine to RM50 million.
Saifuddin said the ministry had subsequently informed Najib that if he paid the reduced RM50 million fine, his release date would be August 23, 2028, while failure to pay would result in a release date of August 23, 2029.
Saifuddin said Malaysia currently had no specific law governing the mechanism for house arrest.
He said he had previously obtained Cabinet agreement in principle to begin the process of introducing a House Arrest Act, but the proposal was initially intended to address prison overcrowding, particularly involving remand prisoners.
Saifuddin said Malaysia currently had 41 prisons housing about 93,000 inmates, against a total capacity of around 75,000.
Under the proposed mechanism, remand prisoners could potentially be placed under house arrest and monitored through modern electronic devices until their trial dates.

Title: AKPS steps up border security readiness ahead Johor Bahru‑Singapore RTS Link launch in January
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) is stepping up its security readiness and border inspection capabilities ahead of the launch of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link in January next year.
AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said preparations were being intensified through the use of technology, personnel training and operational simulations to ensure effective inspection of documents and goods.
He said that despite the important role of technology in supporting enforcement, it could not be regarded as the sole solution to security threats at the country’s entry points.
“Technology helps, but it is not the solution to these threats. A combination of both is essential, while how we utilise technology for enforcement is equally important, including training,” he told Bernama recently.
Mohd Shuhaily said AKPS would also advise operators on suitable technologies to enhance security and mitigate potential risks.
On the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help curb the smuggling of illicit goods, he said the technology needs to undergo a learning phase, including machine learning, before reaching maturity.
“Before AI can mature, it needs to learn through what is known as machine learning. So, it is still a work in progress,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohd Shuhaily said 400 AKPS trainees were currently undergoing a three-month training programme at the Segamat Police Training Centre ahead of their deployment to the RTS Link.
He said the trainees were expected to complete their training by the end of September before being deployed to the RTS Link in October.
“We will conduct dry runs over the remaining two months so that by January, everyone is fully prepared to operate this new facility,” he said.
Mohd Shuhaily said the personnel would initially work alongside senior officers at the Sultan Iskandar Building to gain experience, particularly in inspecting documents and goods. — Bernama

Title: Preliminary report on Sarawak Flying Doctor helicopter crash due within 30 days, says deputy transport minister
Article:
MIRI, Sept 19 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (BSKU) will issue a preliminary report on the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash on September 8 within 30 days of the accident, in accordance with Annex 13 of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) on Aircraft Accident and Incident Investigation.
Deputy Minister for Transport Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the preliminary report would subsequently be presented to the Cabinet, in line with the Cabinet’s decision on September 9.
“BSKU will issue a preliminary report within 30 days from the date of the accident, in accordance with ICAO Annex 13,” he told reporters when met at a function in Long Lama on Saturday (September 19).
Hasbi added that the BSKU was currently conducting a technical investigation in accordance with ICAO Annex 13 and Part XXVI of the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016.
He said BSKU investigators had gone to the crash site to examine the site and aircraft wreckage, as well as collect and preserve evidence.
“The investigation covers examination of the crash site and aircraft wreckage, the collection and preservation of evidence, a review of operational and maintenance records, crew information, weather conditions and other relevant evidence,” he said.
He said the investigation was also receiving technical cooperation and support from the aircraft manufacturer in Germany and the engine manufacturer in the United States, in accordance with ICAO Annex 13.
He stressed that the cause of the accident and any contributing factors had yet to be determined.
“At this stage, the cause and contributing factors of the accident have yet to be determined.
“The investigation is ongoing and BSKU will not draw any conclusions until all the evidence has been examined,” he said.
On September 8, a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crashed at the Long Lellang STOLport at around 3.40pm, killing all five crew members on board.
The victims were identified as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; as well as staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — The Borneo Post

Title: Police seek Interpol help after six foreigners charged with Jalan Ampang Pavilion Embassy robbery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Six foreign men were charged in absentia at the Sessions Court here yesterday with armed gang robbery at a residential unit in Pavilion Embassy here on Sept 7.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the charge was framed under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code, which carry a maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment and whipping upon conviction.
“During yesterday’s proceedings, the Deputy Public Prosecutor applied for arrest warrants for all the accused.
“The court subsequently set Oct 16 for mention of the application for the arrest warrants,” he said in a statement today.
Fadil said police would apply for an Interpol Red Notice to track down and arrest all the suspects.
He said police received a report on Sept 7 from a 28-year-old Chinese national who was robbed at his residence at about 5.31pm.
Fadil said the investigation papers were referred to the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Prosecution Office on Sept 17.
He urged anyone with information on the suspects’ movements or whereabouts to contact the nearest police station immediately to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Cloud seeding operation begins in Klang Valley after API readings exceed 150 for 24 hours
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The government, through the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), will conduct a cloud seeding operation in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya today and tomorrow to mitigate the effects of the haze and improve air quality in the affected areas.
Nadma director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the operation was being carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department, Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), with an RMAF C-130 Hercules aircraft serving as the main asset.
“The cloud seeding operation is scheduled to be conducted on Sept 19 and 20, following Air Pollutant Index (API) readings for PM2.5 in the affected areas exceeding 150 for more than 24 hours, based on readings by the Department of Environment.
“However, the operation is subject to weather conditions and the presence of suitable clouds for the seeding process,” he said in a statement today.
He added that Nadma and the relevant agencies will continue to monitor developments in the haze situation and prevailing weather conditions to ensure that appropriate measures can be coordinated from time to time. — Bernama

Title: Melaka Pakatan finalising talks with Bersatu, others to form PH Plus for state polls
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 19 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) Melaka is finalising negotiations with parties that have similar aspirations, including Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), to form a PH Plus collaboration to contest the Melaka State Election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the negotiations were being conducted based on decisions made at a meeting of the PH Presidential Council
“The negotiations also include Bersatu, but any form of cooperation will only be announced after the negotiation process has been completed,” he told a press conference after attending the launch of Amanah’s election machinery in Duyong here today.
Also present were Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who is also Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, and Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa.
Meanwhile, Adly, who is also Deputy Defence Minister, said the distribution of seats within PH among PKR, Amanah and DAP had been finalised, including the allocation of eight seats to Amanah.
Among the state seats that Amanah are set to contest are Bukit Katil, Durian Tunggal, Telok Mas and Merlimau.
Asked about the possibility of collaborating with Barisan Nasional (BN), Adly said that, so far, no negotiations had been held with the party. — Bernama

Title: Prabowo welcomes Malaysia’s offer of aircraft, helicopters and team to fight Indonesia fires
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has welcomed Malaysia’s offer to assist in tackling forest fires in the country, including through the provision of assets and expertise.
He said the offer involved an aircraft, three helicopters and a firefighting team.
He said this after receiving a courtesy call from Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at the President’s residence in Hambalang, Bogor, on Friday.
“This is an environmental problem that affects many parties and although the fires are in Indonesia, their impact is also felt by our neighbours, so they want to help us and we welcome the assistance,” he said in a video recording uploaded on the social media accounts of Indonesia’s Presidential Secretariat and also shared by Ahmad Zahid on his social media on Saturday.
Prabowo said Indonesia had also received offers of assistance from several other countries, including Japan, to help put out the prolonged forest fires, particularly in Kalimantan.
He said Indonesia was also drawing up comprehensive preventive measures to ensure that the same situation did not recur every few years.
Earlier, Ahmad Zahid, who is currently on a four-day visit to Jakarta, conveyed the offer to Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka on Wednesday.
Malaysia’s offer involves a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).
Prabowo also stressed the importance of maintaining and strengthening Malaysia-Indonesia relations.
He said the meeting also discussed several other matters, including cooperation in the halal industry. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar vows to strengthen pondok schools, introduce AI and modern fields
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 19 — The government will help streamline and elevate pondok institutions (traditional religious schools), including in terms of physical facilities, academic disciplines and the introduction of new fields of study suited to current needs, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The Prime Minister said that, as an initial step, several pondok institutions would be selected to pioneer new traditions of learning based on their respective areas of specialisation and
tarbiah
or disciplines.
“Since independence in 1957, governments have changed, but this is the first time we are truly assisting.
“I want to emphasise this because many people have raised questions. I will not decide what the (pondok) curriculum is, as it is not my field. I am just proposing how to improve its dignity and position, including through new areas of knowledge and disciplines,” he said in his speech at the opening ceremony of the National Turath Scholars’ Consultation, held in conjunction with the Malaysia Islamic Turath Festival 2026, here today.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, former Grand Mufti of Egypt Sheikh Prof Dr Ali Jum’ah Muhammad Abdul Wahab and prominent Moroccan scholar Sheikh Prof Dr Sayyid Idris al-Fasi al-Fihri.
Anwar said pondok institutions also need to be exposed to new disciplines, including artificial intelligence (AI), which he said has great potential as a tool for Islamic outreach and the development of the Muslim community.
“AI is an important tool for Islamic outreach and the revival of Islam, and AI without a system of ethics and morality can become a problem and a major threat that could ultimately harm us.
“There are dangers associated with AI, just as there are with phones and computers. So children in pondok institutions must also be trained to master AI,” he said.
The Prime Minister said efforts to strengthen pondok institutions should also take into account the diverse educational pathways available to their students, adding that not all such institutions necessarily need to produce religious scholars.
“If we say that all pondok institutions must produce religious scholars, that is not possible. Some are specialised (in the religious field).
“Some of them want to go into engineering, want to become pilots, want to venture into TVET (Technical and Vocational Education and Training), I think that is not a problem. At least they have sufficient knowledge and a religious foundation,” he added.
At the same time, Anwar said some pondok institutions need to have pathways to universities to enable their graduates to contribute to the public education system.
“I agree that even if we recognise pondok programmes up to the higher-education level, it does not necessarily mean their graduates must go to university. That is fine. I agree. There is no problem with that.
“But we must remember that for some pondok institutions, having a pathway to university is also important as their graduates will go on to influence the public education system,” he added. — Bernama

Title: MACC says Najib’s conditional pardon has no impact on 1MDB case
Article:
KAJANG, Sept 19 — The status of the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case involving Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak remains unchanged following his conditional pardon, said Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman.
He said each case must be handled separately based on the issues and investigations involved.
“For our part, cases that are still pending will continue as usual. The status quo remains,” he told a press conference here today.
He said this when asked whether the conditional pardon granted to the former prime minister would have any impact on the ongoing 1MDB case and appeal.
Abd Halim said one case could not simply be equated with another, as each investigation involved different allegations and issues.
“We need to understand that each case is different. They cannot be handled as if they were the same case, as each investigation is focused on what is being investigated, whether it concerns specific issues raised or complaints received,” he said.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to grant Najib a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.
The Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department said the decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya, held at Istana Negara yesterday. — Bernama

Title: Perodua Alza driver dies after collision with Volvo trailer lorry near Sungai Tong in Terengganu
Article:
BANDAR PERMAISURI, Sept 19 — A man was killed after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) he was driving collided with a trailer lorry at Kilometre 38 of Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kota Bharu near Sungai Tong here last night.
Setiu district police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the accident at 12.01am and identified the victim as Mohd Assfarizal Salim, 44, of Taman Balok Pelangi, Kuantan, Pahang.
“Initial investigations found that the accident is believed to have occurred at about 11.30pm when the Perodua Alza MPV lost control and entered the opposite lane before colliding with a Volvo trailer lorry.
“The MPV driver was trapped inside the vehicle and was extricated by firefighters before being taken to Setiu Hospital for treatment after sustaining serious injuries. He later died at about 4.10am today,” he said in a statement today.
Zahril Asri said the lorry driver, who was travelling from Jertih to Kuantan, was uninjured, adding that police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged anyone who witnessed the incident to come forward to the Setiu district police headquarters traffic division or contact investigating officer Inspector Aliah Syafinah Ani Sarudin at 013-6706156 to assist with the investigation. — Bernama

Title: MACC records Mat Sabu’s statement in fertiliser supply probe, 37 witnesses called so far
Article:
KAJANG, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has recorded statements from Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu and the ministry’s secretary-general in connection with an investigation into the delays in the supply of fertiliser in Kedah.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Mohamad’s statement was recorded on September 16, while the secretary-general’s statement was recorded a day earlier.
He added that, so far, 37 witnesses had been called and their statements recorded to assist in the investigation, which began on August 26, regarding the appointment of a company by the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM).
“The investigation is still ongoing, and is expected to be finalised within another week or two,” he told a press conference here today.
Abd Halim said the MACC would also record statements from several more witnesses to complete the investigation, which is being conducted under Section 471 of the Penal Code concerning the offence of using documents known or believed to be forged.
He said that, at this stage, MACC believes there are criminal elements and governance-related issues in the case, but is more focused on the criminal aspects.
“We will set aside the governance issues for now because we are focusing on the criminal aspects. However, I cannot comment further because the investigation is still ongoing,” he added.
Previously, MACC’s initial investigation found that a company was supposed to supply 616,015 bags of fertiliser, but until September only 333,655 bags had been supplied, leaving a shortfall of 282,360 bags.
The investigation papers were opened following a complaint regarding allegations that the fertiliser supplier appointed by KPKM failed to supply fertiliser under the Paddy Production Incentive Scheme (SIPP) in areas under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada). — Bernama

Title: MACC directs former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez and family to file asset declarations within one month
Article:
KAJANG, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Anti Corruption Commission (MACC) has issued notices to former Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim and his family members requiring them to declare their assets within a month.
According to
Berita Harian
(BH), MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the notices were handed to Azeez and his children this week under legal provisions.
“We have already served notices on Datuk Seri Azeez and his family to declare their assets within a month as provided under the law. The notices were delivered together with the relevant forms for reporting to MACC,” he told BH at a press conference after officiating an event at Kajang Prison College today.
On September 9, Azeez was charged with one count under Section 23 of the MACC Act.
As of September 18, MACC has charged six individuals in connection with eight cases under the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), while five other investigations remain ongoing.

Title: Three young motorcyclists killed, nine injured as 15 vehicles collide in pre‑dawn Ipoh crash
Article:
IPOH, Sept 19 — Three motorcyclists were killed and nine others injured in a crash involving 12 motorcycles and three cars along Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here early today.
Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the incident was reported at 3.35am,
Harian Metro
(HM) reported.
Preliminary investigations showed all 15 vehicles were heading from Meru towards Tambun when the collision occurred.
“Two motorcyclists aged 19 and 20 were confirmed dead at the scene. Nine others, aged between 19 and 25, who sustained injuries were taken to Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital (HRPB) for treatment,” he said in a statement to HM.
Another 19 year old rider died while receiving treatment in HRPB’s Emergency and Trauma Department, bringing the total fatalities to three.
All three car drivers escaped injury.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. Police are working to establish the cause and sequence of events.
Members of the public with information are urged to contact the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at Ipoh district police headquarters.

Title: MCMC and police trace individuals tied to resurfaced 2018 clip accused of insulting Rukun Negara
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 19 —The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has identified several social media accounts and individuals linked to a viral video of a stage performance that allegedly insults the institution of the Malay Rulers and the Rukun Negara.
In a statement today, MCMC said an initial review found that the recording originated from a 2018 stage performance and has since resurfaced on social media.
“MCMC is also working with the Criminal Investigation Department of the Royal Malaysia Police to complete the investigation, including matters related to digital evidence,” the statement read.
The public has been advised against speculating or spreading unverified information about individuals linked to the video, to prevent the investigation from being disrupted.
Earlier, National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang urged the police and MCMC to conduct an immediate and thorough probe into the stage performance video,and take appropriate action if any laws are violated, taking into account all relevant legal provisions. — Bernama

Title: Thumbprints gave her away: Woman gets four months’ jail for presenting fake MyKad at Sabah NRD
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 19 — A 55-year-old woman who went to the Sabah National Registration Department (NRD) to replace her identity card ended up being arrested after the card was found to be fake.
Jamilah Akrim was sentenced to four months’ jail by Magistrate Dzul Elmy Yunus after pleading guilty to possessing the fake identity card at the Sabah NRD Identity Card Division at about 11.30am on Sept 10.
The court also ordered Jamilah to be referred to the Immigration Department for further action upon completing her sentence.
The court heard that Jamilah presented the card when seeking a replacement, but checks by NRD officers found it did not exist in the department’s records, while her thumbprints also did not match any records in the system.
She was charged under Regulation 25(1)(e) of the National Registration Regulations 1990 (Amendment 2007), which carries up to three years’ jail or a fine of up to RM20,000, or both, upon conviction. — Daily Express

Title: Azalina: Pardon power is part of the law, not above it
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The constitutional power to grant pardons should not be portrayed as placing any individual above the law, Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today.
She said the power of pardon was expressly provided for under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution and was therefore not a power exercised outside the law.
“The principle of the rule of law is not in dispute. No individual, government or institution is above the law.
“However, the Federal Constitution is the supreme law of the country, and all parties are likewise bound by its provisions,” she said in a statement posted on her Facebook page.
Azalina was responding to a statement by the Pakatan Harapan Presidential Council yesterday following the conditional royal pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
She said judicial decisions and the pardoning process were distinct matters, with the courts responsible for determining guilt and sentences, while Article 42 provides a constitutional mechanism for pardons, reprieves and remissions of sentences.
“The existence of the constitutional power of pardon does not mean that a court’s decision is disregarded, nor does it place any individual above the law,” she said.
She added that every institution must act within the powers conferred on it by the Federal Constitution.
“The respective roles of the Pardons Board, the Attorney General and the relevant Minister must be understood in accordance with Article 42 and the prescribed constitutional process, rather than through political interpretation or perception,” she said.
Azalina said questions concerning the validity, legal effect or process of any action should be assessed based on the Constitution, the facts and the actual process followed rather than merely on political statements.
“Respect the decisions of the courts. Respect the Constitution. Respect the processes provided for by the Constitution.
“No one is above the law. And no one is above the Constitution,” she added.
Najib was convicted in 2020 over the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International, a former 1MDB subsidiary, and began serving his 12-year prison sentence in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction.
His original sentence was halved to six years and his RM210 million fine reduced to RM50 million following a review by the Federal Territories Pardons Board in 2024.
Yesterday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with conditions that have not been publicly disclosed so far.
